answer.rationale: The 18% spend cut mandate combined with the 14-day contract cliff creates urgent pressure. Memory_c2 shows that switching to the low-cost vendor achieved sharp unit cost reduction with quick onboarding and reliable invoicing. Memory_c6 demonstrates that the incumbent's multi-year pricing advantage may not be available at renewal given the budget pressure. Verifying c2 and c6 will confirm whether the prior low-cost vendor transition remains viable and whether incumbent renewal pricing can still deliver value. The assembly line's 94% utilization is a material risk factor—switching requires careful vendor validation and 30-day transition monitoring to ensure no delivery gaps. A standard experiment scale allows phased volume transfer rather than immediate full cutover, mitigating integration risk while capturing the cost reduction needed to meet the mandate. This approach preserves uncertainty by avoiding both a hasty full switch and a deferral that wastes the renewal window.
